topic: The WW2 Ghost Army fought with inflatable tanks, sound effects and fake radio
taste: No combat, no Nazi symbols; the enemy is only a pair of binoculars in a bush.

claims.claim: The US Army's 23rd Headquarters Special Troops ('Ghost Army'), about 1,100 men, was a WW2 tactical deception unit.
Many of its men were artists recruited from art schools; members included Bill Blass (later a fashion designer) and Ellsworth Kelly (later a famous painter).
It used inflatable rubber tanks, jeeps and artillery.
It played recorded sound effects of troops and vehicles, and sent fake radio traffic.
Its job was to deceive the enemy about where real Allied units were.
The unit's mission was kept top secret until 1996.
The Ghost Army received the Congressional Gold Medal in 2024.

rejected.claim: Sound effects could be heard 15 miles away.
French civilians saw four soldiers lift a tank.
rejected.reason: Not verified in this check - not narrated.
